PRENATAL CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Centre

QF-PCR RAPID ANEUPLOIDY DETECTION

Patient: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
Hospital No: [redacted ID]
Specimen: Amniotic fluid
Date collected: [redacted date]
Date received: [redacted date]
Date reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL DETAILS
Maternal age: 38 years
Gestation: 16 weeks by ultrasound
Indication: Advanced maternal age - screening for chromosomal trisomies

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
DNA extracted from uncultured amniocytes
Multiplex QF-PCR analysis of short tandem repeat (STR) markers:
- Chromosome 13: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
- Chromosome 18: D18S535, D18S391, D18S390, D18S386
- Chromosome 21: D21S1435, D21S1411, D21S1412, D21S1437
Amplification products analysed by capillary electrophoresis

RESULTS
Chromosome 13: Normal biallelic pattern observed for all informative markers
Chromosome 18: Normal biallelic pattern observed for all informative markers
Chromosome 21: Normal biallelic pattern observed for all informative markers

CONCLUSION
Normal complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. No abnormalities detected.

This QF-PCR result indicates a low risk of trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), and trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) in this pregnancy.

LIMITATIONS
This test only examines chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. Other chromosomal abnormalities, mosaicism below 20%, and structural rearrangements will not be detected.

FOLLOW-UP
Full karyotype analysis of G-banded chromosomes from cultured amniocytes to follow. This will provide comprehensive cytogenetic analysis of all chromosomes.

Authorised by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Date: [redacted date]
